name: Deep Dive — Joint Revocable Trust, Happy Path
query: What does the Brady trust say?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Calls Wealth:find_client with the name the advisor used — not Wealth:get_clients alone
Step 2: Finds two matching households (Brady/CA and Brady-Hollis/TX) and asks which, as a table
Step 3: The disambiguation table has exactly the columns Client, Family name, State, Spouse
Step 4: On the advisor naming California, calls Wealth:list_documents for that household and reads each row's readingState before promising anything
Step 5: Recognises two trusts on file and asks which — in prose, because two items is below the table threshold
Step 6: Calls Wealth:get_executive_summary for the joint revocable trust (wid + vaultId)
Step 7: Presents the summary as prose, attributed to 'the Brady joint revocable trust' with its June 2019 execution date
Step 8: States the extracted-and-unconfirmed provenance in the prose itself
Step 9: Offers both the full-summary upgrade and a deeper estate-risks look, phrased as one question naming both

Step 10: On accepting the estate-risks offer, calls Wealth:get_estate_risks for the SAME document (same wid + vaultId) and reproduces the observation with its citation, framed as a point to discuss, not a finding
Step 11: Offers the disposition diagram next, phrased as a question

Step 12: On acceptance, calls Wealth:get_flowchart(wid, vaultId) scoped to the SAME joint revocable trust vaultId already in hand, and renders the diagram — since get_flowchart is per-document, this diagram may now be asserted as the trust's own
Step 13: Offers the next document by name (the family ILIT)
success_criteria: Client is named in the first sentence of the first substantive answer
Executive summary and estate-risks observation are both prose/reproduced blocks, not tables
Every document-derived statement carries an attribution an advisor would recognise and, where present, an as-of date
Provenance label appears in the answer text, not as a footnote or suffix
The estate-risks observation is framed as a point to discuss and explicitly not a legal review
Exactly one offer per answer, always phrased as a question, never a menu
The diagram is rendered, not described in prose and not tabulated
The diagram is attributed to the joint revocable trust specifically, since get_flowchart(wid, vaultId) is scoped to that document's vaultId
The final offer names the next document explicitly rather than saying 'another document'

Tool sequence is Wealth:find_client (1x) then Wealth:list_documents (1x) then Wealth:get_executive_summary (1x) then Wealth:get_estate_risks (1x) then Wealth:get_flowchart (1x, with the joint revocable trust's vaultId)

Zero calls to get_document_info, get_estate_roles, get_estate_flow, get_estate_plan_data, get_estate_baseline, get_balance_sheet, confirm_document_split, get_estate_snapshot, or get_lookback_report — none of these exist in the live registry (get_estate_snapshot was this skill's earlier, unscoped call, since superseded by get_flowchart)
must_not: any email, phone number, street address, date of birth, or account identifier in the disambiguation table
any tool name, field path, or internal label in advisor-facing text
a document identifier in place of a document name
presenting the extracted trust card as verified or confirmed
the words report, scenario, what-if, estate flow, or legal review in any offer
stating or implying the plan is sound because only one thing was observed
a table with a single row
proceeding with either Brady household without the advisor choosing
